messages:
alicia: Hey, quick one — trying to find logs for a request_id in prod (req=abcd-1234, trace=trace-0a1b). Console request search returned nothing. Best practice for k8s services?

ben: If you have the request_id try Request Explorer first (Console -> Requests). It expects the exact header we propagate (X-Request-ID). Example query: req.id:abcd-1234. If that fails, fall back to pod logs.

sophie: For pod logs, I usually use stern (streaming) or kubectl + grep. Quick commands:
```
# list pods
kubectl get pods -l app=my-service -n prod

# one-off fetch and grep
kubectl logs <pod-name> -c my-container -n prod --since=30m | grep abcd-1234

# streaming (easier when live)
stern my-service -n prod --container my-container | grep abcd-1234
```
That finds the lines where the request id was logged.

ben: If you have trace id, go to Console -> Traces and paste the trace id (trace-0a1b). Traces often show a span with the request header that contains request_id. If the service injects a different header (X-Redwood-Req or x-rw-req) try those values in Request Explorer.

alicia: Thanks — console search gave no hits because the header our gateway sets is X-Redwood-Req, not X-Request-ID. Is there a quick way to map trace->req when the request header differs?

sophie: Yep — two ways: 1) Look at ingress (envoy) logs for the trace id to see the forwarded header. 2) Use the internal CLI helper that correlates traces to logged request ids:
```
# internal helper (available to platform team)
redwoodctl correlate --trace trace-0a1b --namespace prod
# prints matched request_ids and pod/prefix where they show up
```
If you don't have redwoodctl, grep the ingress pods (namespace ingress) for the trace id or for "X-Redwood-Req:"

ben: Another tip — our logging middleware logs both trace and request ids in the same line in JSON. You can do a jq filter on multiline logs:
```
kubectl logs <pod> -n prod --since=1h | jq -R 'fromjson? | select(.req_id=="abcd-1234" or .trace=="trace-0a1b")'
```
If logs are not JSON, use grep and context (-C) to capture surrounding lines.

alicia: Helpful. One more: any quick dashboard link I can paste for others?

sophie: Yes — handy to paste both links: Request Explorer and Trace view. Example patterns (replace ids):
https://console.redwood.com/requests?query=req.id%3Aabcd-1234
https://console.redwood.com/traces?query=trace-0a1b

ben: If you keep hitting sampling gaps (trace exists but not all spans), search for the trace id across logs instead of relying on trace viewer sampling.

alicia: Got it. Found it in ingress logs under X-Redwood-Req. Thanks! :thumbsup:
